title: Half-total-variation bound for a zero-sum indicator sum
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $a : \alpha \to \bbr$ be a real-valued function whose entries sum to zero, $\sum_{x \in \alpha} a(x) = 0$. Then for every subset $S \subseteq \alpha$,
\[
  \Bigl|\sum_{x \in S} a(x)\Bigr| \;\le\; \tfrac{1}{2} \sum_{x \in \alpha} \abs{a(x)}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: the entries of $a$ sum to zero
replaced:
If $a : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $\sum_x a(x) = 0$, then for every $S \subseteq
\alpha$,
$\bigl|\sum_{x \in S} a(x)\bigr| \le \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_x |a(x)|$.
